messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: switched to Eigen FFT
parts:
Thanks for the reminder about Eigen FFT, Ben.
And thanks for help understanding FFT, Matt.

I switched Stan over to the Eigen wrapper of
Kiss FFT. It simplifies licensing and the code
for autocorrelation itself is a fair bit cleaner (none
of that ugly C manage-your-own-memory stuff to
encapsulate and a direct use of std::complex rather
than Kiss FFT's home-brew complex struct).

This required moving the FFT code from the
unsupported Eigen distro into
stan/lib/Eigen. That's going to need to be done
manually every time we update the Eigen libs.

Eigen does a redundant (for us) normalization step
that we don't need because we divide by variance
anyway.

I also renamed the function from "auto_correlation"
to "autocorrelation".

There's a unit test with usage in

stan/test/prob/autocorrelation.hpp

The broken builds are probably because of how Daniel's
sped up the tests by foregoing a clean build each
time. The problem is that it leads to false positives
for problem warnings from Jenkins. At 4 AM, he's
rebuilding fresh -- that fixed the problem last night
without a new check in. He's going to look into whether
this can be automated in some faster way without sacrificing
test accuracy.

- Bob
